title: AIVTuber Stream Scenario
description: Versioned, seeded stream workload definition (issue #70). A scenario describes temporal phases - idle, normal, burst - so the benchmark, soak, retention and quality suites share one realistic workload instead of each inventing its own. Generation is deterministic: scenario identity, scenario_version and seed fully determine the ordered event trace, and logical_start is a declared constant rather than the wall clock. Scenarios carry no message content and no privileged events.

schema_version.description: Scenario document contract version. An incompatible version is refused rather than reinterpreted, and starts a new comparison baseline.

scenario_id.description: Stable scenario identity. Combined with scenario_version it forms the benchmark dataset id.

scenario_version.description: Bumped when the workload changes in a way that makes older traces incomparable. The version is mixed into the generation seed, so a bump reshuffles the trace instead of silently reusing a previous baseline.

scenario_class.description: Workload family. The validator refuses a scenario whose parameters contradict its class, so coverage is checkable rather than asserted. `asset_churn` and `repeated_cancellation` are deliberately absent until the #40 fault overlays can express them.

provenance.description: What kind of claim these parameters support. Synthetic distributions must never be presented as measured production facts.

provenance_note.description: Required human statement of the scenario's basis. A workload that cannot say where its numbers came from should not be checked in.

seed.description: Deterministic generation seed. The trace is a pure function of scenario identity, version, seed and phases.

logical_start.description: Declared UTC start instant, second resolution, no zone offset. A constant rather than the wall clock, so a trace reproduces anywhere. Fractional seconds are refused: two documents declaring the same instant must generate the same trace.

stream_duration_ms.description: Represented stream duration. Must equal the sum of phase durations; an unrepresented tail would make the trace unaccountable.

name.description: Phase name, unique within the scenario, so assertions can name the phase they mean.

duration_ms.description: Phase duration. The events_per_minute ceiling is set so an event can always be given its own millisecond.

events_per_minute.description: Mean event rate across the phase. 0 is a genuine idle phase and contributes no events. Capped at 60000 events/minute, which is the format's own representability ceiling: one event per millisecond, so observed_at can stay strictly increasing and a consumer can tell two events apart. This is NOT a statement about what any runtime can play. Whether a workload is playable is a consumer property, so it is checked by the consumer that has to run it (the cached replay path behind replay-benchmark refuses a denser mixed workload) and not by this document contract, which stays shared by the benchmark, soak, retention and quality suites.

kind_mix.description: Relative weight per event kind. `operator.command` is absent by construction: a synthetic privileged event would have to fabricate its authorization, so operator and failure overlays belong to the #40 fault slice.

semantic_mix.description: Relative weight per semantic band. A hit names an axis the starter index is built from, a near_miss names an off-axis qualified intent, and a miss names no axis at all.

priority_mix.description: Relative weight per priority bucket. Buckets, not raw floats, so a scenario states intent.

distinct_actors.description: Viewer pool size. Repeated-viewer behaviour is drawn from this pool.

distinct_topics.description: Topic pool size, which drives semantic reuse.

repeat_viewer_probability.description: Share of events that reuse the previous viewer, modelling someone who keeps talking rather than a fresh arrival each time. Resolved as an exact quota per phase - floor(events * this value) repeated events, spread evenly - not an independent coin flip per event, so the number of fresh viewers a document produces is exact rather than an expectation that varies with the seed.
